stories.headline: Claude Code “Don’t Ask Again” feature leaves passwords in public GitHub files
stories.in_brief: Researchers found 1,122 public GitHub copies of Claude Code’s .claude/settings.local.json file that contain passwords, API keys or other secrets. The leak occurs when users select “Yes, and don’t ask again,” causing the assistant to store the exact command—including any secret—in the project settings file.
stories.so_what: The discovery highlights a risk for developers using Anthropic’s Claude Code AI assistant, as the saved settings file can be inadvertently committed to version control and become publicly accessible. Because the file is not automatically added to a project’s .gitignore, older commits and forks retain the secrets even after the file is removed, requiring a full rotation of compromised credentials. Security firm Apiiro identified 1,122 public copies of the file containing at least one secret such as database passwords, SSH logins or GitHub tokens. Organizations should audit repositories for the .claude/settings.local.json file, revoke any exposed credentials, and implement stricter git‑ignore policies to prevent future leaks.
stories.what_to_do: 1. Search all repositories for the file .claude/settings.local.json and remove any instances. 2. Rotate every password, API key, token or secret that may have been stored in the file. 3. Add .claude/settings.local.json to the project’s .gitignore and ensure global git excludes are configured on all developer machines.

stories.headline: SonicWall Issues Patch for SSL‑VPN MFA Bypass Vulnerability CVE‑2026‑19868
stories.in_brief: SonicWall released updates fixing a CVE‑2026‑19868 flaw that lets attackers bypass SAML‑based MFA on its SSL‑VPN, and CISA has listed the bug as exploited in the wild. The advisory urges immediate upgrade of affected SonicOS firewalls.
stories.so_what: The vulnerability affects SonicOS SSL‑VPN services that rely on SAML authentication, allowing a user with valid alternate credentials to sidestep multi‑factor controls. With a CVSS score of 7.1, the flaw is considered high‑severity and has been added to the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, confirming real‑world abuse. Federal agencies must remediate by 20 November 2026, and SonicWall recommends all customers install the patched versions (7.3.4‑7013 for Gen7 and 8.2.3‑8015 for Gen8). No workarounds exist, and the same advisory also addresses six other flaws, two of which score 8.8 and could permit unauthenticated actions. Organizations should verify they are not running the vulnerable firmware, apply the updates promptly, and monitor for any anomalous VPN activity as the threat landscape around SonicWall appliances remains active.
stories.what_to_do: 1. Identify SonicOS firewalls running Gen7 7.3.3‑7015 or earlier, or Gen8 8.2.2‑8015 or earlier. 2. Upgrade to SonicOS 7.3.4‑7013 or 8.2.3‑8015 as soon as possible. 3. Verify that SAML‑based login is disabled or secured until the patch is applied.

stories.in_brief: OpenAI has reportedly raised $11 billion in a new financing round that values the company at $1.25 trillion. The partial round could close at roughly $20 billion, remaining below earlier targets.
stories.so_what: The infusion of $11 billion provides OpenAI with capital to continue expanding its AI services while the market for artificial intelligence remains volatile amid regulatory concerns and shifting investor sentiment. Although the round values the firm at $1.25 trillion, it represents only about 37% of the $30 billion originally sought, indicating tighter funding conditions for AI firms. Investors will watch whether the round expands to the projected $20 billion and how the valuation compares with rivals such as Anthropic, whose prospective IPO valuation has been revised downward. The outcome may influence the timing of OpenAI’s planned public offering and affect shareholders of partner companies like Microsoft and Nvidia that rely on OpenAI’s growth.

stories.headline: NASA Opens Applications for New Astronaut Class Ahead of Artemis Missions
stories.in_brief: NASA announced that applications are open until Dec. 3, 2026 for its next astronaut class, aiming to expand the Artemis program. The agency plans to select candidates by late 2027 to train for lunar and future Mars missions.
stories.so_what: The opening of applications marks a critical step as NASA seeks to increase its astronaut corps from the current 32 active members to support the Artemis program’s goal of returning humans to the Moon and eventually sending crews to Mars. With a deadline of 11:59 p.m. EST on Dec. 3, 2026, U.S. citizens with a master’s degree in a STEM field can apply, reflecting NASA’s emphasis on technical expertise and diverse experience. The agency expects to make its final selection in late 2027, with training beginning in early 2028, aligning with the planned Artemis IV lunar landing near the south pole. Observers will watch the applicant pool size, selection criteria, and how the new class integrates into upcoming lunar missions and the broader goal of establishing a sustainable Moon presence.

stories.headline: NASA APOD Features Widely Reported European Fireball Meteor on Nov 8, 2026
stories.in_brief: NASA’s Astronomy Picture of the Day on November 8, 2026 displayed a major fireball meteor captured over the Dolomite Alps. The event was extensively reported across Europe and linked to the Northern Taurid meteor shower.
stories.so_what: The fireball’s appearance highlights the ongoing activity of the Northern Taurid stream, which originates from dust left by Encke’s comet and can produce bright meteors visible over large regions. Its widespread sightings, documented by the American Meteor Society and the International Meteor Organization, provide valuable data for tracking meteoroid trajectories and assessing potential future impacts. Astronomers will monitor the Taurid stream in the coming weeks to refine models of its debris field and improve forecasting of similar events. The APOD image also offers the public a visual reminder of Earth’s dynamic space environment and the importance of coordinated observation networks.

stories.headline: Apple and Meta Join 67 Firms Objecting to OKX‑ICE Tokenized Stock Venue
stories.in_brief: Apple and Meta Platforms added their objections to OKX‑ICE’s tokenized‑stock platform, bringing the total number of objecting issuers to 67. The move blocks the venue from listing tokenized versions of these companies’ shares under the SEC’s innovation exemption.
stories.so_what: The objections by Apple and Meta complete a sweep of the so‑called “Magnificent Seven” tech giants, which together represent a large share of the S&P 500’s value. Under the SEC’s innovation exemption, a written objection within 30 days prevents a venue from offering a tokenized version of a company’s stock, limiting OKX‑ICE’s ability to launch a broad range of tokenized U.S. equities. With major megacaps now excluded, the joint venture between Intercontinental Exchange and OKX may have to focus on smaller or less‑known issuers, potentially reducing the appeal of its 24/7, blockchain‑based trading model. Observers will watch which, if any, remaining large‑cap stocks the platform can list and whether other crypto‑friendly firms choose to object or participate.
